title: Violetta Rebrand
summary: A modern identity for a family interior design studio: a rose growing from a V, refreshed without losing its heritage.

hero.alt: Two Violetta business cards on a sunlit kerb: a gold card with the debossed rose logo on top of a white card reading “Violetta Interior Design Studio.”

sections.heading: Client Overview
body: Violetta is a long-standing interior design business with deep roots in family tradition. Passed down through generations, it has kept its core values of refinement and luxury. As the market modernised, Violetta needed a refreshed identity that balanced contemporary aesthetics with that heritage.

media.alt: The original Violetta Interior logo in gold foil on black: a rose inside a serif V.
media.caption: The original logo.

sections.heading: The Challenge
body: Redesign Violetta’s logo and visual identity to appeal to a modern audience while keeping the elements of the original logo that carry its family legacy. The rebrand also needed symbolic elements, such as floral motifs, that tell the brand’s story of perseverance and elegance.

sections.heading: 1. Logo Redesign: Balancing Tradition and Modernity
body: The original logo featured a rose inside a “V”, symbolising the brand’s name and its floral identity. To modernise it while keeping its essence, I:
– Simplified the lines of the rose and the “V” for a cleaner, more contemporary look.
– Kept a serif typeface (Reckless Neue) as a nod to the original, reinforcing maturity and timelessness.
– Embedded symbolism: the “V” acts as both a vase (nurturing growth) and a shield (protection and resilience), and the rose growing out of it stands for renewal, mirroring the brand’s journey.

sections.heading: 2. Colour Palette: Luxury with a Vintage Touch
body: To convey refinement and warmth, the palette is led by golds (#DAAC00, #FFE687) taken from the original logo. A light blue (#6B82FF) is used sparingly for contrast, balancing vintage charm with modern sophistication.

sections.heading: 3. Typography: Classic Meets Contemporary
body: Headings: Reckless Neue, a modern serif that honours the original logo’s lettering while feeling fresh.
Body text: DM Sans, a clean sans-serif that stays readable across digital and print.

sections.heading: 4. Graphic Devices: Reinforcing the Story
body: Floral motifs: the rose becomes patterns and standalone graphics that build recognition.
Fluid shapes: organic, hand-crafted shapes that suggest adaptability and bespoke service.

sections.heading: Applications
body: The identity was applied across several touchpoints:
– Debossed business cards, for a tactile, luxurious feel.
– Instagram: a curated feed that pairs high-end interiors with storytelling captions.
– Posters and print: minimal but striking designs that show off the refined aesthetic.

media.alt: A row of Violetta posters on a brick wall by a street, with gold and blue panels, the rose logo and the line “01 Interior Design Done Right.”
media.caption: Poster series.

media.alt: Mock-up of an Instagram post for Violetta: a pale yellow square with the wordmark, placeholder text and the rose logo.
media.caption: Instagram template.

sections.heading: Results and Impact
body: Stronger recognition: the modernised logo stays familiar to long-time clients while attracting new audiences.
A cohesive visual language: colour, typography and symbolism work together as one brand experience.
Emotional connection: the embedded meanings (rose, shield, vase) tie the brand back to its heritage.
